The graph of the function $f(x),$ which is defined on $[0,10],$ is shown above. It consists of line segments.

Find the average value ${f}_{\text{avg}}$ of $f(x)$ on $[1,9].$ Do not round the answer.

${f}_{\text{avg}}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The average value of a function on a given interval $[a,b]$ is 

$$
{f}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the additive property of the definite integral, we write

$$
{\int }_{1}^{9}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{5}^{9}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}.
$$

The 1st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [1,5].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot 2 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{1}=-4.
$$

The 2nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [5,9].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot 3 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have 

$$
{\int }_{5}^{9}f(x)\,\text{d}x={A}_{2}=6.
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{9}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-{A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =-4+6 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the formula for the average value, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{9-1}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
